paragraph: The Livro Branco das TIC 2023-2027 was [approved by Presidential Decree 272/24 of 5 December 2024](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2025/decreto-presidencial-n-o-256-25-de-03-de-dezembro/>). The approval [repealed the Livro Branco das TIC 2019-2022](<https://www.mondaq.com/telecoms-mobile-cable-communications/1585472/white-paper-on-information-and-communication-technologies-2023-2027-strategic-vision-for-icts-in-angola>). In the last twelve months, a March 2026 article cited the policy as [setting plans for a space studies centre and expert training](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/angola-launches-259-million-earth-observation-satellite-project>). It was cited and not changed. The ministry's site carries only [Presidential Order 129/19 of 22 July 2019, with a download link](<https://minttics.gov.ao/ao/documentos/despacho-presidencial-129-19/>), which approved the earlier white paper. No source found says whether the 2023-2027 text is public. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public.

In November 2023 the project PAFEN [called for consultants to evaluate the national ICT development policy and draft a new one for 2025-2034](<https://pafen.gov.bi/recrutement-dun-bureau-detudes-charge-de-levaluation-et-de-la-mise-a-jour-de-lapolitique-nationale-de-developpement-des-technologies-de-linformation-et-de-lacommunication-ainsi-que-de-lelabo/>). The policy it would replace was [adopted by the Council of Ministers on 13 July 2011](<https://primature.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/politique_nationale_developpement_tic.pdf>) and [ran from 2010 to 2025](<https://primature.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/politique_nationale_developpement_tic.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says the 2025-2034 policy has been drafted, validated or adopted, and no text of it is known. Establishing would need a sector policy that is adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

No stage is set. The Déclaration de politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique ran to 2021. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on a mandated body, finance or a report against the policy's targets. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption, or a successor in preparation now that the period has ended.

No stage is set. The ministry published the Politique sectorielle de l'Economie numérique et des Postes 2016-2020 in September 2015, and its period ended in 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a successor sector policy has been announced, drafted, validated or adopted. Nothing has been found on a delivery plan, reporting or finance for the 2016-2020 policy. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

Botswana's National Assembly [approved the policy in August 2007](<https://publicadministration.un.org/unpsa/Portals/0/UNPSA_Submitted_Docs/2019/f912b59f-5963-4335-9dff-194a1a522c49/Maitlamo%20Policy_26112019_083359_d807e512-ea2e-4d56-8fba-60679904b985.pdf>). The Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology [published the full text](<https://publicadministration.un.org/unpsa/Portals/0/UNPSA_Submitted_Docs/2019/f912b59f-5963-4335-9dff-194a1a522c49/Maitlamo%20Policy_26112019_083359_d807e512-ea2e-4d56-8fba-60679904b985.pdf>) that month. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A report of December 2025 [refers to it as Botswana's existing policy](<https://www.ids.ac.uk/publications/biometric-digital-id-in-africa/>). Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan or a report against its targets. No source of finance has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's own targets.

No stage is set. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is named for the Central African Republic, and no source found says whether one has been adopted, is in preparation or does not exist. No dated source found says the country has none. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

No stage is set. No ICT sector policy has been found for Côte d'Ivoire, whether adopted, in preparation or expired. The only instrument found is the national digital strategy, the [Stratégie nationale de développement du numérique en Côte d'Ivoire (SNNCI 2021–2025)](<https://www.ids.ac.uk/publications/biometric-digital-id-in-africa/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

No stage is set. The Stratégie sectorielle des postes, télécommunications et TIC was finalised at a seminar in September 2005, and its targets ended in 2015. No source found states that it was adopted by decree or by the minister. No successor sector policy is on record as adopted or in preparation. No text, report against it, responsible body or budget line has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

No stage is set. The Document de politique sectorielle of 2009 ran out in 2014 without its review. In the last twelve months, on 4 August 2026, the minister of the digital economy said [the government validated the Sectoral Policy of the Digital Economy](<https://augustinkibassa.cd/2026/08/04/rdc-s-e-augustin-kibassa-lance-la-politique-sectorielle-de-leconomie-numerique-et-la-strategie-nationale-de-lia-pour-batir-un-congo-souverain-connecte-innovant-et-inclusif/>). It sets guidelines to 2030, and adoption by the Council of Ministers is the next step. Nothing has been found on the 2009 text, the cost of its 2015 targets, reporting, governance or finance. Establishing would need a sector policy that is adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

The government [drew up its national ICT development policy in 2008-2009](<https://leonjusteibombo.cg/2023/02/22/congo-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-6-mars-2019/>), the minister told the Council of Ministers on 6 March 2019. An [appraisal document of 4 May 2011 treats the National ICT Policy as existing](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/123451468204842891/pdf/616460PAD0P1220e0only0900BOX358354B.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether the policy's text was published, when and by what act it was adopted, or what period it covers. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

In September 2022 the minister for posts, telecommunications and the digital economy told the ITU's plenipotentiary conference that [Comoros was in the process of implementing](<https://pp.itu.int/2022/en/itu_policy_statements/kamalidini-souef-comoros/>) the Politique sectorielle des télécommunications et du numérique. The ministry's mission page, dated to 2016, [names the new sector policy beside the Comores numérique strategy](<https://minpoten.egouv.km/fr/ministry/mission/>). Nothing on the policy is dated after September 2022, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. No text, adoption date, period, delivery plan or report against it has been found. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

No stage is set. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is on record for Cape Verde as adopted, in preparation or absent. A national digital strategy is held instead. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found that names a sector policy, its text, its period or a body responsible for it. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

In July 2025 the minister [drew on the Politique nationale de développement des TIC to report progress on the digital divide](<https://communication.gouv.dj/djibouti-porte-sa-vision-dun-numerique-inclusif-au-sommet-mondial-sur-la-societe-de-linformation-2025/>) at the WSIS Forum. The Schéma stratégique intégré, [approved by a law published in February 2015](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/arabe/texte-juridique/loi-n80-an-14-7eme-l-portant-approbation-du-schema-strategique-integre-ssi-du-secteur-des-technologies-de-linformation-et-de-la-communication-tic-en-republique-de-djibouti/>), covered the sector before it and [ran for ten years, from 2014 to 2024](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/arabe/texte-juridique/loi-n80-an-14-7eme-l-portant-approbation-du-schema-strategique-integre-ssi-du-secteur-des-technologies-de-linformation-et-de-la-communication-tic-en-republique-de-djibouti/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No text of the new policy has been found, and nothing gives its adoption date, period, costs or budget line. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

No stage is set. The one sector instrument found for Algeria is a ministry's [Plan d'action du secteur de la poste et des télécommunications](<https://www.indjazat.com/karim-bibi-triki-ministre-de-la-poste-et-des-telecommunications-plus-grandes-sont-les-realisations-plus-grands-sont-les-defis/>). No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation, and no dated statement that the country has none has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

No stage is set. The National ICT Strategy 2013-2017 reached the end of its period in 2017, and no sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation after it. The ministry's web page gives the ICT 2030 Strategy a period, to 2030, and nothing else. No source found says whether it was adopted, is being drafted or was only announced. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

[The UNECA paper of April 2009](<https://archive.uneca.org/sites/default/files/PublicationFiles/03_harmonization_tic-final_en.pdf>) states that Eritrea has no national ICT policy defining the government's orientation and strategies for development. [The same paper](<https://archive.uneca.org/sites/default/files/PublicationFiles/03_harmonization_tic-final_en.pdf>) states that no National ICT Development Plan exists. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing later confirms or contradicts the paper. Nothing has been found on governance or finance. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

Ethiopia's National ICT Policy and Strategy was [developed in 2016](<https://unctad.org/system/files/official-document/BRI-Project_RP21_en.pdf>) and [endorsed by the Council of Ministers in 2017](<http://www.ist-africa.org/home/default.asp?docid=8216&page=doc-by-id>), with [financial support from the World Bank](<http://www.ist-africa.org/home/default.asp?docid=8216&page=doc-by-id>) for the 2017 revision. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated account, from September 2021, has the policy [still being implemented](<https://unctad.org/system/files/official-document/BRI-Project_RP21_en.pdf>). No source found says whether the policy's text is published or what period it covers. Establishing would need the text to be public and the period not ended.

[A JICA baseline study of public service digitalisation in African countries was published in March 2022](<https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12369203.pdf>). It states that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy, the Politique nationale des TIC, consistent with the PSGE Vision 2025, and gives no date of adoption. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing on the policy is dated since. The policy's text, period, delivery plan, reporting, mandated body and finance have not been found. Establishing would need an adopted policy with its text public and its period not ended.

The Ministry of Communications [released the National Telecommunications Policy as final on 10 January 2005](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/National-Telecommunications-Policy-NTP-2005.pdf>), and the [full 33-page text](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/National-Telecommunications-Policy-NTP-2005.pdf>) is on the National Communications Authority's website. The policy [states no end date for itself](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/National-Telecommunications-Policy-NTP-2005.pdf>). A report published on 8 October 2025 [recommends updating it and the ICT for Accelerated Development Policy of 2003](<https://researchictafrica.net/research/digital-africa-post-the-pandemic-ghana-report/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report against the policy's targets, no cost for its actions and no source of finance has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the policy's own targets.

In June 2024 the national digitalisation strategy [announced a digital sector policy letter](<https://ande.gov.gn/file/2025/01/Strategie-Numerique_Guinee-2027_v1.2.pdf>) and [lists it as a document still to be drafted](<https://ande.gov.gn/file/2025/01/Strategie-Numerique_Guinee-2027_v1.2.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 9 July 2026, the digital economy ministry [opened a national workshop to draft a telecommunications policy, strategy and action plan](<https://agpguinee.com/guinee-tenue-dun-atelier-delaboration-de-la-politique-de-la-strategie-et-du-plan-daction-des-telecommunication-2026-2030/>), with support from the World Bank's WARDIP project. The policy [is to cover 2026 to 2030](<https://agpguinee.com/guinee-tenue-dun-atelier-delaboration-de-la-politique-de-la-strategie-et-du-plan-daction-des-telecommunication-2026-2030/>). The government [adopted an ICT policy and strategy in 2010](<https://smartafrica.org/IMG/pdf/srategie_tic_finale_v.6_28_juillet_2016.pdf>). No source says the new policy has been validated or adopted. Establishing would need it adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

The ICT4D Policy Statement 2018-2028 [runs from 2018 to 2028](<https://publicadministration.desa.un.org/sites/default/files/list-of-files/2025/1.2.1%29%20data%20governance%20-mocde.pdf>), as the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy's presentation titles it. The presentation [lists the statement among the country's existing policies, strategies and legal frameworks](<https://publicadministration.desa.un.org/sites/default/files/list-of-files/2025/1.2.1%29%20data%20governance%20-mocde.pdf>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in October 2026 a Principal Assistant Secretary at the ministry [named it among The Gambia's ICT policies](<https://times.co.sz/45787/news/gender-checks-proposed-for-digital-policies/>). No source found links or quotes its text, and none says it is unpublished. Nothing has been found on a delivery plan, a mandated body or finance. Establishing would need the text to be public.

[An ICT strategy was in preparation in Guinea-Bissau in December 2021](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P177016084979202b08dd501a5690c82506.pdf>), when the regulator, ARN, issued a preliminary report on it. The Guinea-Bissau Digital Economy Diagnostic, published in 2022, [takes data from the regulator's preliminary ICT strategy report](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P177016084979202b08dd501a5690c82506.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated since shows whether drafting continued. No source says the strategy was adopted. No text, period, delivery plan, responsible body or finance has been found. Establishing would need a sector policy that is adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

No stage is set. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found for Equatorial Guinea as adopted or in preparation. No dated statement that the country has none has been found. Nothing has been found on a mandated body, finance, a delivery plan or a report. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

Kenya's ICT Sector Policy Guidelines 2006 [were reviewed and updated to a National ICT Policy in 2019](<https://ict.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-04/Final%20Communications%20Policy%20as%20at%2022nd%20January%202026.pdf>). The policy [was gazetted in 2020](<https://cms.icta.go.ke/sites/default/files/2022-04/Kenya%20Digital%20Masterplan%202022-2032%20Online%20Version.pdf>) as Gazette Notice No. 5472. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. An analysis of July 2026 [names the ICT policy among Kenya's existing instruments](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/strengthening-legal-and-policy-frameworks-for-ai-accessibility-for-persons-with-disabilities-in-kenya/>). A Communications Authority consultation of September 2026 says the policy [directs government agencies to promote and license private investment in carrier-neutral data centres](<https://www.ca.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-09/Public%20Consultation%20on%20Data%20Centres%20September%202026.pdf>). Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan or a domestic budget line. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's own targets.

Liberia's government [adopted the policy in 2019](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/2026-Liberia-Data-Governance-Policy-REVISED-CIPESA-1.pdf>), and the [full text is on the ministry's website](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/ApprovedNationalICTPolicy2019-2024Liberia.pdf>). It [was extended to 2025](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/2026-Liberia-Data-Governance-Policy-REVISED-CIPESA-1.pdf>), and the ministry's draft of its successor, dated 7 January 2025, [lists it as expired](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/NATIONAL-ICT-POLICY2025-2030Draft-1-Jan-7-2025.docx.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the national digital strategy of 3 February 2026 said the successor [has been drafted and is in consultation, with approval targeted for the last quarter of 2025](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Liberia-National-Digital-Strategy.pdf>). A press release of 8 September 2026 [lists a draft National ICT Policy](<https://www.einpresswire.com/article/939735610/csquared-completes-commercial-broadband-programme-in-liberia-with-support-from-microsoft>). No adoption of the National ICT Policy 2025-2030 is on record. Establishing would need an adopted policy whose period has not ended.

In October 2025 the General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GACI) [announced root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi](<https://libyaherald.com/2025/10/general-authority-for-communications-and-informatics-libya-enters-digital-sovereignty-era-with-official-launch-of-root-servers-in-tripoli-and-benghazi>). It [presented them as implementing the National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027](<https://libyaherald.com/2025/10/general-authority-for-communications-and-informatics-libya-enters-digital-sovereignty-era-with-official-launch-of-root-servers-in-tripoli-and-benghazi>). In the last twelve months, on 15 February 2026, GACI held a workshop in Tripoli. There officials [stated the aim of drafting legislation and a guidance manual for data centres and cloud computing](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=351103&lang=ar>). No text of the strategy has been found, and no source says whether it is published. No adopting act, delivery plan or budget line has been found. Establishing would need the strategy's text to be public.

The government [adopted the policy in 2008](<https://www.gov.ls/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Final_Communications_Policy_Document.pdf>), and the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology [published the full text](<https://www.gov.ls/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Final_Communications_Policy_Document.pdf>). The Lesotho Communications Policy [states no end year or review date](<https://www.gov.ls/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Final_Communications_Policy_Document.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. A 2025 tender notice says the ministry [will review the policy with the authority](<https://selibeng.com/consultancy-services-for-review-of-the-lesotho-communications-policy-2008-and-communications-act-2012/>). No delivery plan and no report against the 2008 policy has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the policy's own targets.

No stage is set. The Note d'orientations générales du secteur des télécommunications à horizon 2023 was adopted on 26 December 2019 and ran to 2023. No successor note has been found as adopted or in preparation. No report against its targets and no finance for it has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

The MPTDN formulated the Politique nationale des TIC pour le développement in 2004 [with support from UNDP](<https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12369203.pdf>). A JICA study of March 2022 describes it as [the Malagasy government's main ICT policy](<https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12369203.pdf>), and found that [legal and regulatory reform was relatively advanced](<https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12369203.pdf>). Its targets run to [2015 for the digital network](<https://openjicareport.jica.go.jp/pdf/12369203.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months; the latest account is JICA's. The policy's text, an act adopting it and a stated period have not been found, so no source says whether it is still open. Establishing would need its text to be public and its period not ended.

The Government [adopted the national information and communication technology policy in 2005](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Mali/Nacionalnaa%20strategia%20razvitia%20cifrovoj%20ekonomiki%202020%20prinata%20v%202015.pdf>), after adopting the Déclaration de politique sectorielle des télécommunications [in 2000](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Mali/Nacionalnaa%20strategia%20razvitia%20cifrovoj%20ekonomiki%202020%20prinata%20v%202015.pdf>). The strategy Mali Numérique 2020, of November 2014, [sets out the 2005 policy's six priorities](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Mali/Nacionalnaa%20strategia%20razvitia%20cifrovoj%20ekonomiki%202020%20prinata%20v%202015.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No text of the 2005 policy has been found, and no source says it is unpublished. No period, delivery plan, results report, mandated body or budget line has been found. Establishing would need the text to be public.

[The Council of Ministers approved the Política para a Sociedade da Informação on 20 March 2018 by Resolution 17/2018, in force from 21 June 2018](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_122_I_SERIE_2018.pdf>). [The full text is printed in the Boletim da República, I Série, no. 122, of 21 June 2018](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_122_I_SERIE_2018.pdf>). The policy [states no end date and no review year](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_122_I_SERIE_2018.pdf>). In April 2026 Mozambique [told a UNCTAD ministerial roundtable](<https://unctad.org/system/files/non-official-document/ecn162026_s08_mr_mozambique_miquidade_en.pdf>) that the policy aims at widespread adoption of ICT. The statement names no change to it, so it was cited and not changed in the last twelve months. No report against the policy's own targets has been found. Operating would need results published against those targets.

The ministry's presentation of April 2019 states that [a new sector policy declaration was adopted in January 2013](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/Workshops-and-Seminars/bsg/2019040405/Documents/Presentation%204.pdf>). It [gives the declaration's four pillars](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/Workshops-and-Seminars/bsg/2019040405/Documents/Presentation%204.pdf>). Nothing on the declaration is dated after April 2019, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. Its text has not been found. Nothing gives its period, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body or a budget line. Establishing would need the text to be public and the period not ended.

No stage is set. The National ICT Policy 2007-11 was issued in September 2007 and ended in 2011. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. The National ICT Strategic Plan it relies on has not been found. No report against the policy has been found, and no change in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

Malawi's National ICT Policy 2013 is [listed in the policy framework of a 2025 management plan for the government data centre](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099083025102027538/pdf/P505095-7a647ee6-33d5-44b5-97c1-1c135c16efd2.pdf>). An essay of March 2026 [links a copy of the 2013 policy's text in the ITU national strategies repository](<https://data-landscapers.com/2026/03/31/africa-data-problem/>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A GSMA report of August 2026 [lists the National ICT Policy 2013 among prior policies](<https://www.gsma.com/about-us/regions/africa/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Driving-digital-transformation-of-the-economy-in-Malawi.pdf>). The Presidential Delivery Unit [produced a draft National ICT and Digitalization Policy in 2022](<https://www.intgovforum.org/en/filedepot_download/258/21450>). No source says it was adopted. No delivery plan of the 2013 policy has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's targets.

In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the Ministry of ICT [launched the policy at Opuwo](<https://www.namibian.com.na/ict-ministry-launches-strategic-plan-policy-to-expand-digital-access-and-strengthen-cybersecurity/>), and the minister said it [would guide the ICT sector over the next five years](<https://www.namibian.com.na/ict-ministry-launches-strategic-plan-policy-to-expand-digital-access-and-strengthen-cybersecurity/>). It follows the Overarching ICT Policy 2009 and the earlier National ICT Policy / Broadband Policy, to which the ITU's repository gives [a time frame of 2018 to 2022](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>). The text of the National ICT Policy 2026 has not been found, and its period has no end year. No delivery plan, report against it or budget line is on record. Establishing would need the text to be public.

No stage is set. The Document de politique sectorielle des télécommunications et des TIC 2013-2020 ended in 2020. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation, and an update instructed in July 2017 has not been found. The [Politique nationale du numérique 2021-2030](<https://www.mfwa.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/RAPPORT-FINAL-NIGER_April-1-.pdf>) was also found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on the policy's text, a mandated body or its finance. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.
